claims.head: The Ducks hit, the Sabres mostly don’t
claims.body: On physicality, Anaheim is one of the league’s best, but Buffalo is near the bottom. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Ducks.

claims.head: Forecheck against patience
claims.body: The Ducks hound the puck, but the Sabres sit back. Anaheim is near the top of the league for forecheck pressure, and Buffalo is near the bottom. Expect the Ducks to win more pucks back deep in the Sabres’ end.

notes.text: Rasmus Dahlin returned in their last game after missing 3 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Dennis Gilbert was added to the roster on Oct 14 and has played beside Louis Crevier.
Jason Zucker was added to the roster on Oct 22 and has played beside Josh Norris and Konsta Helenius.
Zach Metsa has started killing penalties: on the ice for 48% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, up from 7% last season.
Josh Norris has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, up from 1% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 23% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

ANA.head: A slightly uphill night for the Ducks
ANA.body: Even though Anaheim has home-ice advantage, the Ducks will be without Terry, and Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Ducks’ best way to tip it is a penalty kill that holds up.

BUF.head: Leaning the Sabres’ way
BUF.body: Even though Anaheim has home-ice advantage, the Ducks will be without Terry, and Buffalo has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Ducks can still swing it if their penalty kill holds up.
